L0@P0: arXiv:2102.07392v1 [math.AG] 15 Feb 2021
L1@P0: PLURIPOTENTIAL THEORY FOR TROPICAL TORIC VARIETIES
L2@P0: AND NON-ARCHIMEDEAN MONGE–AMPERE EQUATIONS `
L3@P0: JOSE IGNACIO BURGOS GIL, WALTER GUBLER, PHILIPP JELL, AND KLAUS ´ KUNNEMANN ¨
L4@P0: Abstract. Tropical toric varieties are partial compactifications of finite dimensional real
L5@P0: vector spaces associated with rational polyhedral fans. We introduce plurisubharmonic
L6@P0: functions and a Bedford–Taylor product for Lagerberg currents on open subsets of a tropical toric variety. The resulting tropical toric pluripotential theory provides the link to give
L7@P0: a canonical correspondence between complex and non-archimedean pluripotential theories
L8@P0: of invariant plurisubharmonic functions on toric varieties. We will apply this correspondence to solve invariant non-archimedean Monge–Amp`ere equations on toric and abelian
L9@P0: varieties over arbitrary non-archimedean fields.
L10@P0: Contents
L11@P0: 1. Introduction 1
L12@P0: 2. Forms and currents 7
L13@P0: 3. Plurisubharmonic functions on partial compactifications 13
L14@P0: 4. Bedford Taylor calculus on a partial compactification 20
L15@P0: 5. Semipositive metrics and θ-psh functions 23
L16@P0: 6. Toric Monge–Amp`ere equations 32
L17@P0: 7. Monge–Amp`ere equations on totally degenerate abelian varieties 43
L18@P0: 8. Monge–Amp`ere equations on arbitrary non-archimedean abelian varieties 52
L19@P0: Appendix A. Proof of Theorem 6.2.13 61
L20@P0: References 63
L21@P0: 1. Introduction
L22@P0: Pluripotential theory is a non-linear complex counterpart of classical potential theory.
L23@P0: It is the study of plurisubharmonic (short: psh) functions and the complex Monge–Amp`ere
L24@P0: equation. There are rich applications to multidimensional complex analysis, K¨ahler geometry, algebraic geometry and to dynamics. A celebrated result was Yau’s solution [Yau78]
L25@P0: of the complex Monge–Amp`ere equation for smooth forms on a K¨ahler manifold more than
L26@P0: twenty years after Calabi proved uniqueness. Bedford and Taylor [BT82] showed that one
L27@P0: can go beyond the smooth case as there is a well-defined product for the positive (1, 1)-
L28@P0: currents associated to locally bounded psh functions and hence the Monge–Amp`ere measure
L29@P0: makes sense for such functions. Later, Demailly [Dem93] defined also a Bedford–Taylor
L30@P0: product for singular psh functions. Here, singular means that the functions ϕ are allowed
L31@P0: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary 32P05; Secondary 32U05, 14T90, 32W20.
L32@P0: Key words and phrases. Pluripotential theory, tropical toric varieties, tropicalization of abelian varieties,
L33@P0: non-archimedean Monge–Amp`ere equations.
L34@P0: J. I. Burgos was partially supported by MINISTERIO DE CIENCIA E INNOVACION research projects
L35@P0: PID2019-108936GB-C21 and ICMAT Severo Ochoa project CEX2019-000904-S. W. Gubler, P. Jell and
L36@P0: K. K¨unnemann were supported by the collaborative research center SFB 1085 Higher Invariants - Interactions between Arithmetic Geometry and Global Analysis funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft.
